items.question: Which finding identifies the vessel leaving the left ventricle as the aorta at screening?
options: Its anterior wall is continuous with the ventricular septum and it does not divide
It divides after a short course
It is larger than the other great artery
It runs to the left of the other great artery
items.explanation: The vessel from the left ventricle has its anterior wall continuous with the septum and does not bifurcate.

items.question: Which finding identifies the pulmonary artery?
options: It arises from the right ventricle and divides after a short course
It gives off the head and neck vessels
Its wall is continuous with the ventricular septum
It is always smaller than the aorta
items.explanation: The pulmonary artery arises from the right ventricle and branches after a short course.

items.question: How do the two great arteries normally relate to each other as they leave the heart?
options: They cross, the pulmonary artery almost at right angles to the aorta
They run parallel, side by side
They join into one trunk
The aorta lies in front and to the left
items.explanation: The great arteries cross each other; the pulmonary artery crosses the ascending aorta at almost a right angle.

items.question: Which great artery is usually slightly larger in fetal life?
options: The pulmonary artery
The aorta
They are always exactly equal
It alternates through the cardiac cycle
items.explanation: The pulmonary artery is usually slightly larger than the ascending aorta in fetal life.

items.question: One great artery is clearly much smaller than the other. What does the guideline say?
options: A major discrepancy should lead to further evaluation
This is the normal slight difference
It matters only if the four-chamber view is abnormal
It should be rechecked after birth
items.explanation: The great arteries should be approximately equal in size; a major discrepancy should lead to further evaluation.

items.question: In the rotational technique, which way is the transducer rotated from the four-chamber view to open the left outflow tract?
options: Towards the fetal right shoulder
Towards the fetal left hip
Towards the fetal spine
It is not rotated; it is slid towards the feet
items.explanation: From the four-chamber view the transducer is rotated towards the fetal right shoulder.

items.question: What is the best record of the relationship between the two outflow tracts?
options: A cine clip
One still frame
A measurement of each valve
A written note
items.explanation: The relationship of the two outflow tracts is best shown on cine clips, not still frames.

items.question: Which lesions does the left outflow-tract view help to identify that the four-chamber view does not show?
options: Outlet septal defects, conotruncal abnormalities and aortic valve abnormalities
Abnormal abdominal situs
Atrial size discrepancy
Pericardial effusion
items.explanation: The LVOT view helps identify outlet ventricular septal defects, conotruncal abnormalities and aortic valve abnormalities not visible in the four-chamber view.

items.question: Are sagittal views of the aortic and ductal arches part of the routine cardiac screen?
options: No: they are not currently part of the routine screening examination
Yes: both are mandatory
Yes: the aortic arch only
Only when colour Doppler is used
items.explanation: Sagittal arch views and assessment of the neck vessels are not currently part of the routine cardiac screening examination.

items.question: What should the aortic and pulmonary valves look like?
options: Moving freely and not thickened
Thick and bright
Fixed in the open position
Not visible at screening
items.explanation: Each semilunar valve should move freely and should not be thickened.
